nonLabourLines.description: Staging/CI infrastructure and cloud hosting (staging + prod slots) for pipeline setup
Stripe integration testing, sandbox and PCI-related tooling
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / temporary environment for 400k+2M record migration
Contingency buffer (~10% of labour) for a single-FTE, placeholder-rate estimate

assumptions: The rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour with 1 FTE available. All costs are therefore purely indicative until real roles (e.g. Backend Engineer, Frontend Engineer, QA, DevOps, PM) and their market hourly rates are assigned to named team members.

No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; this estimate is built solely from backlog story points converted to effort hours using an industry-standard assumption of ~6.5-7 hours of delivery effort per story point (covering design, build, test, review, and deployment), which is itself an assumption given the lack of team composition detail.

With only 1 FTE available on the single placeholder role, the team is staffed far too thinly to deliver all 24 backlog items in parallel or within a short timeframe; total estimated effort of ~3,373 hours represents roughly 1.9 person-years of work for one full-time person, implying a calendar duration of ~20+ months if no additional headcount is added. This is flagged as a major staffing risk.

Story points were converted using a rough mapping: 1 point ≈ 6.5 hours, adjusted upward slightly for high-complexity/high-risk items (e.g. legacy data migration, payment integration, multi-currency) to reflect integration, testing and compliance overhead not captured by points alone.
Priority breakdown sums labour cost only, allocated pro-rata by each task's story points within its priority band, using the single Team member rate.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for infrastructure, third-party tooling, and audit support commonly needed for these backlog items (CI/staging environment, Stripe sandbox, data migration tooling, accessibility audit) plus a general contingency buffer given the high uncertainty of a placeholder rate card.

Total story points across the backlog: 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21+8+8+5+5+8+13+8+5+8+13+8+8+5+8+5+8 = 205 points, translating to ~3,373 hours of effort at ~16.45 hours/point average (higher for complex urgent/high items like PW-7, PW-8, PW-14).

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) and Payment provider integration (PW-7, 13 points) are treated as higher-risk/higher-effort-per-point items due to real-world integration, data-quality and compliance complexity beyond typical story-point estimation.
Scenario range (optimistic/most likely/pessimistic) reflects uncertainty inherent in point-to-hour conversion and the unresolved rate card/staffing situation, not variance in scope.
GDPR (PW-9) and two-factor authentication (PW-17) are treated as High priority compliance/security items requiring careful implementation and testing, consistent with their listed priority.
input.reasoning: "Effort was derived from the 24 backlog items' story points (total 205 points) using an approximate conversion of story points to delivery hours (~16.45 hours/point on average), adjusted upward for complex items such as legacy data migration, payment integration and multi-currency support to reflect real-world integration and compliance overhead beyond a linear points-to-hours mapping. This produced a most-likely total of ~3,373 hours. Because the rate card contains only one placeholder role ('Team member' at 75 USD/hour, 1 FTE), all effort was costed against that single line, producing a most-likely labour cost of ~253,000 USD. Non-labour costs were added for infrastructure, third-party tooling and an audit for accessibility compliance, plus a contingency buffer given the high uncertainty from the placeholder rate card and single-FTE staffing constraint. Three scenarios (20th/50th/80th percentile) were provided to reflect estimation uncertainty: the optimistic case assumes lower per-point effort and no major surprises in legacy migration or payment integration; the pessimistic case assumes migration and integration complexity runs higher than typical, plus schedule inefficiencies from single-FTE staffing (context switching, no parallelism). Priority breakdown apportions labour cost across Urgent/High/Medium/Low bands based on each task's share of story points within that band. This estimate should be treated as a rough order-of-magnitude figure only, to be revisited once actual roles, rates and headcount are defined and once any historical actuals become available."
